subject.title: [Feature]: Compaction: configurable model override + flush-then-reset mode

question: Should OpenClaw add a default-off compaction-threshold flush-then-reset mode, and should it share policy with reset-time agentic memory flushing in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/45608?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the remaining gap, but the feature changes config surface, silent model execution, provider/auth routing, durable memory writes, and session reset semantics, so automation should not choose the product and security defaults alone.

options.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
options.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset-after-flush with explicit, daily, and idle reset memory behavior before implementation.

options.title: Approve default-off resetAfterFlush
options.body: Add a narrow opt-in `memoryFlush.resetAfterFlush` mode with explicit provider, timeout, notification, audit, and regression proof requirements.

options.title: Reject automatic reset after flush
options.body: Keep compaction as the context-preservation path and rely on model overrides, memory flush, and manual resets for cost control.

recommendation.title: Design unified reset-memory policy first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and align compaction-threshold reset-after-flush with explicit, daily, and idle reset memory behavior before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to both the original pre-compaction memory flush and the memoryFlush.model override, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product/security decision.
